verdict.rationale: Resend's own docs say developers can build email templates with React using React Email and send them through the API. Hands-on community users independently confirm that React-based templates work. Because the templates are code, they can live in version control, though the docs never describe that workflow. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party React Email documentation beyond a single llms.txt line, explicit documentation of a version-controlled template workflow, and a statement that Resend maintains React Email first-party.

support.subject: As a developer, I can author emails as code — React Email, MJML, or an equivalent maintained framework the vendor documents first-party — and keep templates in version control

citations.quote: Build email templates with React using [React Email](https://react.email), then send them through the API.
Being able to create email templates in React is great, too.
